query: A Spring Boot 3.4 service (Java 21, Maven, Spring Data JDBC, PostgreSQL in production) has an OrderService with a DiscountPolicy collaborator and an OrderRepository. Write (1) a unit test class verifying the discount is applied before saving, with no real database, and (2) an integration test class verifying an order can be persisted and read back through the real repository. Also state how the integration tests are kept out of the fast mvn test run.
expected_behavior: Unit test uses @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) with @Mock/@InjectMocks (no openMocks, no imperative mock())
All assertions use AssertJ (assertThat), never JUnit's assertEquals/assertTrue
Every test method has a method-level @DisplayName whose camelCase mirror is the method name, behavior-phrased (shouldDoXWhenY), and no class-level @DisplayName appears
Integration test uses Testcontainers PostgreSQL (not H2), wired via @ServiceConnection on a static @Container field
Integration test class is named *IT and/or @Tag("integration"), with Failsafe vs Surefire separation explained
Removes the class-level @DisplayName and adds a method-level one in natural language
Renames testGet to a behavior-focused name mirroring the @DisplayName (no test prefix)

query: Our integration suite is slow and flaky: every IT class declares its own non-static @Container PostgreSQLContainer, several tests pass only when run in order because earlier tests insert rows they rely on, and someone proposed switching the suite to H2 to speed it up. What do you change?
expected_behavior: Rejects H2 — keeps the real production engine via Testcontainers, citing dialect/SQL-fidelity risk
Makes containers static and shares one container across the whole suite (singleton or Spring-managed @TestConfiguration bean), referencing the lifecycle reference for the pattern
Removes inter-test order dependence via per-test state isolation (transaction rollback in slices, or truncate/Flyway reset)
Does not disable or skip any failing tests
